name: SAP CIAM
abstract: SAP Customer Identity and Access Management (SAP CIAM), formerly Gigya and SAP Customer Data Cloud, is a multi-tenant SaaS customer identity platform on SAP Business Technology Platform. It covers registration and login (password, social, passwordless with FIDO passkeys, phone, email OTP, and magic links), two-factor and risk-based authentication, consent and preference management, and B2B contact and partner management. SAP CIAM can act as an OpenID Connect provider (authorization code, implicit, hybrid, client credentials, device, and token exchange flows) and relying party, and as a SAML identity provider and service provider. Sites are hosted in United States, European Union, Australian, or Chinese data centers, with global site groups for cross-region SSO. Pricing is subscription-based per block of 10,000 monthly active users, with optional enhanced security and consent add-ons.

features.description: Login, registration, and password management are included in the B2C Core plan.
Social Login lets users identify with their social networks; custom OpenID Connect and SAML providers can also be added as login buttons in screen-sets.

FIDO authentication is offered as a passwordless login method on mobile devices and common desktop browsers; the accounts.auth.fido.login method supports conditional mediation for discoverable credentials.
Email OTP login sends a one-time code to the user by email; it requires email as the site login identifier.
Phone Number Login provides passwordless authentication with a one-time code sent to the mobile phone; an SMS provider must be configured.
Magic Link login emails a link that signs the user in; it is driven by the accounts.auth.magiclink.email.send and login APIs and requires a trusted landing page URL and a magic link email template.

Push authentication is a verification method that requires a configured Firebase application and a push-based risk-based authentication rule set.
Risk-Based Authentication rules decide which verification method (email, phone, TOTP, or push) applies to a session, and can trigger reCAPTCHA based on a risk score.

Two-factor verification is documented for both user logins and profile updates, with the method driven by the auth level of the configured risk-based authentication rules.
The platform can act as an OpenID Connect provider (authorization code, implicit, and hybrid flows) and as a relying party for third-party providers.

The web browser SSO profile is supported with HTTP POST and HTTP Redirect bindings; the platform can act as a SAML identity provider for any number of service providers, or as a SAML service provider.

The platform can act as a SAML service provider for external identity providers, and as a SAML identity provider for external service providers.

The OIDC provider supports the authorization code flow, along with implicit and hybrid flows using the code, token, and id_token response types.
Refresh tokens are issued (for example in the device flow) and can be used to obtain a new access token, ID token, and refresh token; they keep the permissions of the original token.
Requests go to the token endpoint with grant_type, client_id, and client_secret; only an access token is returned, without refresh or ID tokens.
The implicit flow is supported with the id_token and token response types.
RFC 8693 token exchange can reduce or extend the permission scopes of an existing token, and supports an actor_token to add an act claim for single-level delegation.
